questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"In Sami's family, everybody has a job at home. His father cooks on Fridays, his mother checks the homework, his sister does the shopping and Sami washes the dishes. Nobody does everything, and nobody does nothing."

What is the main idea of this passage?

options.text: Sami's father is a very good cook.
All the family share the housework.
Sami's mother works too much at home.

questions.explanation: Every sentence supports one idea: each member has a job, and the last sentence sums it up — nobody does everything. So the family share the housework. "Sami's father is a very good cook" takes one detail (he cooks on Fridays) and adds a judgement the text never makes. Sami's feelings and his mother's tiredness are not mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The school science club meets twice a week. On Tuesday the members do experiments in the lab, and on Thursday they prepare their projects for the end-of-year fair."

What do the members do on Thursday?

options.text: They do experiments in the lab.
They clean the lab after the experiments.
They prepare projects for the fair.
They sit for a test in the lab.

questions.explanation: Scan for the key word "Thursday" and read its whole sentence: "on Thursday they prepare their projects for the end-of-year fair". "They do experiments in the lab" is the Tuesday activity — the trap of the first day you meet. Cleaning and a test are not mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Karim switched off the television, put his school bag by the door and yawned. Then he set his alarm clock for six and turned off the light."

What is Karim most probably about to do?
questions.explanation: The text never says "sleep", but the clues prove it: he yawns, sets his alarm and turns off the light. "Go to school" tempts because of the school bag, but he puts it by the door for the next morning — the alarm is for six. He has just switched off the television, so he is not watching a film.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Doctors say that walking is excellent for your health. It is free, and you can do it almost anywhere."

In the second sentence, what does "it" refer to?
questions.explanation: "It" is singular and names something you can "do" and that is "free": put the noun back — "walking is free, and you can do walking almost anywhere". "Your health" is the nearest singular noun, but you cannot "do" your health. "The doctors" is plural.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Mum was happy: the room was spotless. There was not a single bit of dust, and every book was in its place."

What does the word "spotless" most probably mean?
questions.explanation: The next sentence explains the word: no dust at all, and everything in its place — the room is very clean. The parts of the word help too: "spot" + "less" means without any spot. "Very dirty" is the opposite, and the text says nothing about the size or the light of the room.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The bus was late, so we missed the beginning of the film."

What is the function of the linker "so" in this sentence?

options.text: It introduces the cause of the delay.

questions.explanation: "So" opens the consequence: the late bus is the cause, missing the film is what follows from it. It does not introduce the cause — that needs "because" (We missed the film because the bus was late). A contrast needs "but" or "whereas".
